sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4.32 billion in FY2016 to $34.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was a step change, not a straight line: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, fell 3.9% in FY2023, then grew 13.7% and 34.3% in the last two years [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].

The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which brought $2.4 billion of cash and $1.6 billion of short-term investments and made Embedded revenue $4.55 billion against $246 million in FY2021 [P37][P41][S110][S109].
FY2025 growth was driven by Data Center and Client and Gaming, with Data Center revenue up 32% to $16.6 billion on EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs [P15][S98].
Data Center was the largest driver, contributing 15.7pp of FY2025's 34.3% growth and 48.0% of revenue [D694][D483][D692].
Client and Gaming added 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client at $10.6 billion and Gaming at $3.9 billion [D701][S124][S127].
Client revenue rose 51% on a 31% increase in processor unit shipments and a 15% increase in average selling price, and Gaming rose 51% on higher semi-custom revenue and Radeon GPU demand [P10][P9].
Operating income grew 94.4% against 34.3% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Operating costs grew 10.0pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 24.3% [D512][D504].
Operating margin of 10.7% in FY2025 sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
Gross margin reached a window high of 49.5%, up 0.2pp, as cost of revenue added only 0.2pp to operating margin while SG&A took 1.2pp off [F40][D800][D498][D513][D515].
The gross margin gain came from product mix, partly offset by about $440 million of net inventory and related charges tied to the MI308 export control [P14].
In FY2025 net margin of 12.5% sat 1.9pp above the 10.7% operating margin, helped by $577 million of other income and a $103 million tax benefit [F80][F60][D843][X123][X113].
Operating cash flow of $7.71 billion was 1.78x net income in FY2025, above the 1.61x window median, and free cash flow was 1.55x net income [F110][F70][D470][D833][D471].
Operating cash flow rose on $4.3 billion of net income plus $4.6 billion of non-cash adjustments, partly offset by a $2.2 billion inventory build for Data Center products [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% is near the 19.6% window high, with capex at 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A [D467][D803][D466][D472].
Stock-based compensation of $1.64 billion was 21.2% of operating cash flow, down from 46.3% in FY2024 [X83][D473][D416].
Net cash reached $6.46 billion, or 18.6% of revenue, against a -17.3% peer median and in the 100th percentile of five semis peers [D476][D477][D845][D844].
Total debt rose to $4.10 billion after $1.5 billion of notes were issued in March 2025, while cash and investments grew 105.6% to $10.6 billion [D475][P6][D474][D507].
Buybacks of $1.32 billion were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D478][D479][D506].
The current ratio of 2.85x is a window high, above the 2.19x median [F210][D812][D813].
Revenue fell 3.9% in FY2023, the only decline in the window, on a 25% drop in Client revenue and a 9% drop in Gaming [D370][P35].
The decline was a PC inventory correction rather than a structural loss of share, and revenue has since grown 13.7% and 34.3% [P34][D426][D483].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4.10 billion, but net cash still rose to $6.46 billion [D475][D418][D476].
The leverage increase is modest against the cash build and does not threaten the balance sheet.
The effective tax rate moved -21.3pp to -2.5% in FY2025 on an $853 million release of uncertain tax positions [D469][D412][P4].
The tax benefit flatters FY2025 net margin and is unlikely to repeat, so the underlying earnings base is lower than reported.
Whether Data Center revenue growth holds above the FY2025 32.2% rate, reported in the FY2026 10-K, would confirm the AI-driven trend [D693].
Whether operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median or slips toward the 1.8% FY2023 low, reported in the FY2026 10-K, would signal whether the FY2025 recovery is durable [D795][F58].
Whether inventory days stay below the FY2025 165 days or rise further, reported in the FY2026 10-K, would show whether the Data Center build is clearing [D481].
